blocks.text: NATHAN THE PROPHET, AT THE COURT OF DAVID AND SOLOMON · UNITED KINGDOM
Nathan. The promise of David's house, “Thou art the man”, and Solomon's anointing.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
United kingdom c. 1050–930 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
David · Solomon
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
The word came at night: “it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan”; what he told David is called “all this vision”.
THE CALL
How the word came
The word came at night: “it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan”; what he told David is called “all this vision”. 2 Samuel 7:4 2 Samuel 7:17

From the textHis first answer to David, “Go, do all that is in thine heart”, was given before the word came that night; the word that came said that David would not build the house. 2 Samuel 7:3–5 2 Samuel 7:12–13
He was sent: “the LORD sent Nathan unto David”, and he began with a story put to the king as a case to judge. 2 Samuel 12:1–6
Chronicles names a written record, “the book of Nathan the prophet”, for the acts of David and of Solomon. 1 Chronicles 29:29 2 Chronicles 9:29
The title of Psalm 51 sets the psalm “when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba”. Psalms 51:1

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS

From the textScripture does not tell of Nathan's death. His last scene is Solomon's anointing; afterwards he is named only as the writer of a book and in Hezekiah's day. 1 Kings 1:45 2 Chronicles 9:29 2 Chronicles 29:25
TRADITION SAYS

“A grave at Halhul, near Hebron, is pointed out as that of Nathan, but this is doubtful.”[51] Who says so: E. G. Hirsch and E. N. Calisch, Jewish Encyclopedia, 1905; the earliest source has not been identified
Hebron's antiquities are said to include “the tombs of Gad, Nathan the prophet, Abner”.[45] Who says so: A local tradition at Hebron, listed in the Jewish Encyclopedia, reported 1904
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
The LORD sent Nathan, who gave the name
A. F. Kirkpatrick (1881); the Pulpit Commentary (1880–1897)

Kirkpatrick: “Jehovah commissioned Nathan … to give the boy a second name, which he did accordingly.” The Pulpit Commentary: “the sense plainly is that God sent a message by Nathan.” 2 Samuel 12:25 [71][97]
David put the child in Nathan's hand
“Some commentators”, following the Latin Vulgate, as reported by Kirkpatrick and the Pulpit Commentary
They read “he (David) committed him to the hand of Nathan” for his education. Kirkpatrick calls this explanation “doubtful”, with “no further trace of the fact”. 2 Samuel 12:25 [71][97]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no father, tribe or home for Nathan, and does not tell how he became a prophet.
2 Samuel 12:25 does not say plainly who sent Nathan or who gave the name Jedidiah (see the question above).
Chronicles tells Nathan's promise to David (1 Chronicles 17) but not the parable or his part in Solomon's anointing.
Scripture does not itself say that Absalom's deed (2 Samuel 16:22) fulfilled Nathan's word about David's wives (2 Samuel 12:11).
This Nathan is a different man from Nathan the son of David (2 Samuel 5:14; Luke 3:31).
